A vector of values in (0, 1), made by a sigmoid, that scales another vector entry by entry to decide how much passes through.
Gaussian error linear unit, z Phi(z) with Phi the standard normal CDF: a smooth ReLU that dips to about -0.17 near z = -0.75. Used in transformers.
How well a model performs on new examples it was not trained on.
Updating the weights for one state also changes the estimates for similar states, so the agent can value states it has never visited.
A GAN: a generator G(z) and a discriminator D(x) trained against each other; D separates real from fake, G tries to fool D.
A model of the data distribution itself, used to produce new examples that look like the training data (autoencoder-based VAEs, GANs, diffusion models).
A function containing yield, or an expression like (x x for x in xs). Calling it runs nothing; each next() runs the body to the next yield. It can be read only once.
In a GAN, the network G that maps noise z ~ N(0, I) to a fake sample G(z).
1 - sum c p c^2 for class fractions p c: the chance two random draws from the node have different classes. 0 when pure, 0.5 at a 50/50 split of two classes.
The standard version control tool; it stores a project's history as a chain of commits.
nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1): averages each channel over all positions, turning (N, C, H, W) into (N, C, 1, 1) for any H and W.
A point whose value is less than or equal to the value everywhere.
A website that runs Python notebooks on a Google computer. Part 2 of Round 1 is solved in it.
Generative pretrained transformer: a decoder-only model pretrained by next-token prediction.
Graphics processing unit: a processor that runs thousands of arithmetic operations in parallel; PyTorch calls an NVIDIA GPU 'cuda'. Round 2 uses Colab's L4.
The program that scores a Part 2 submission: it imports your file, calls your function or class on hidden inputs, and checks results, imports, banned names, time and input mutation.
The vector of all partial derivatives of a scalar function. It points in the direction of steepest increase and has the shape of the input.
Boosting in which each new tree is fit to the negative gradient of the loss (the residuals, for squared error) and added with a small learning rate.
Comparing a hand-derived derivative or gradient with a numerical estimate such as the central difference, to catch mistakes.
Rescaling all gradients together so their total L2 norm is at most max norm, keeping their direction: torch.nn.utils.clip grad norm (params, max norm), between backward() and step().
Minimizing a loss by repeating w <- w - lr gradient: step against the gradient, which points uphill.
How max pooling backpropagates: each output's gradient goes to the input that was the max of its window (the first one on ties in PyTorch); other inputs get 0, and overlapping wins add up.
torch.amp.GradScaler: multiplies the loss by a large factor before backward and divides the gradients by it before the step, so float16 gradients do not underflow.
L = D - W for a similarity matrix W and the diagonal matrix D of its row sums; v^T L v = (1/2) sum W ij (v i - v j)^2.
An algorithm that makes the best choice at each step without looking ahead, such as choosing tree splits one node at a time.
Always choosing the most likely next token (argmax). Deterministic; prone to repetition.
A policy that picks argmax a q(s, a) in every state for a given action-value estimate q.
Trying every combination of listed hyperparameter values.
A small RL test environment: an agent moves up, down, left or right between the cells of a grid.
The group of users a file belongs to; the second set of permissions applies to its members.
A split that keeps all examples from one group (one patient, one user) on the same side.
A convolution with groups=g: input and output channels are split into g groups and each output group reads only its input group. Weight (C out, C in/g, k, k), so g times fewer weights.
GQA: G key/value heads (G divides H); each group of H/G consecutive query heads shares one. G = H is MHA, G = 1 is MQA.
Gated recurrent unit: an RNN with update and reset gates and no separate cell; h t = (1 - z) n + z h (t-1). 3(HI + H^2 + 2H) parameters per layer.
The weight w in classifier-free guidance: 0 ignores the condition, 1 is plain conditional, larger follows it more closely with less variety.
The standard Python library of RL environments: env.reset() returns (obs, info); env.step(a) returns (obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info).
The set of points on one side of a line, such as {(x, y) : a x + b y + c = 0}.
A fluent but false statement produced by a language model, such as an invented function argument.
Drawing a layer's weights with variance 2/C (C inputs) when its inputs come out of a ReLU, so the output variance matches the input variance.
The last part of a network, usually one nn.Linear, that turns features into the task's outputs (for example class logits). Replaced when the task changes.
Git's name for the commit you are on, usually the newest commit of the current branch. HEAD~1 is the commit before it.
The PDE u t = alpha u xx for the temperature u(t, x) of a rod; alpha 0 is the diffusivity.
The square, symmetric matrix of second partial derivatives of a scalar function; the multivariable version of f''.
A file whose name starts with a dot, such as .gitignore; ls shows it only with -a.
A layer between the input and the output; the data never says what its values should be.
Variables left in the runtime's memory by cells run earlier, run out of order, or since deleted. It makes a notebook work on your screen but fail when run fresh.
The vector h t an RNN carries from step to step: its summary of the sequence so far. nn.RNN returns all of them (out) and the last one (h n).
Clustering that builds a tree of nested clusterings; cutting the tree at a height gives one clustering.
max(0, 1 - y f(x)) for labels y in {-1, +1}: zero outside the margin, growing linearly inside it and on the wrong side.
A plot that cuts the range of a variable into equal-width bins and draws a bar for the count in each; it shows the shape of a distribution. plt.hist(x, bins=20).
Your own directory, /home/ followed by your user name, written ~. cd with no argument goes there.
Roughly how many steps ahead a discounted agent cares about, 1 / (1 - gamma): 10 for gamma = 0.9, 100 for gamma = 0.99.
The name or address of a computer on a network, such as gpu01.example.org.
0.5 e^2 for e <= delta and delta ( e - 0.5 delta) beyond: quadratic for small errors, linear for large ones. nn.HuberLoss(delta=1.0).
A self-supervised speech encoder (Meta): raw 16 kHz waveform in, one vector per 20 ms frame out; pretrained by predicting cluster ids of masked frames.
The Python library of pretrained transformer models; Auto classes plus from pretrained load a model and its tokenizer by name or from a local folder.
An algorithm for the one-to-one assignment of minimum total cost; DETR uses it to match predicted slots to ground-truth objects.
A setting chosen before training that training does not change, such as the polynomial degree, k in kNN, or the learning rate.
A parameter is identifiable when different values of it produce different data; in y = p q x only the product p q is.
I: the square matrix with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere; I x = x, the matrix of the do-nothing map.
The target value (default -100) that nn.CrossEntropyLoss and F.cross entropy skip; the mean is taken over the other positions.
Independent and identically distributed: independent draws from the same distribution.

Subtracting each channel's mean and dividing by its standard deviation, (x c - mean c)/std c; pretrained ImageNet models expect mean [0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std [0.229, 0.224, 0.225] on the [0, 1] scale.
A dataset of about 1.2 million photos in 1000 classes; most pretrained image models were trained on it.
Unable to be changed in place: ints, floats, bools, strings, tuples and None.
A score of how mixed the classes in a tree node are: 0 for a single class, largest for an even mix (Gini or entropy).
Filling missing values with estimates, such as the training median of the column.
A language model adapting to a task from examples in its prompt, with no change to its weights.
An operation that overwrites an existing array instead of making a new one, such as x -= m or x[mask] = 0. On a function's input it changes the caller's data.
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B): the overlap is counted twice, so subtract it once.
Updating an average in place: mean <- mean + (x - mean) / n; with a constant step alpha instead of 1/n it tracks a moving target.
Random quantities are independent when knowing some of them tells you nothing about the others; then E[XY] = E[X] E[Y], and the variance of a sum is the sum of the variances.
Events with P(A and B) = P(A) P(B); knowing one happened does not change the probability of the other.
The row labels of a Series or DataFrame, shown at the left of a printout. By default 0, 1, 2, ...; filtering keeps the original labels.
pandas combines two Series by matching index labels, not positions; a label found in only one of them gives NaN.
The random variable that is 1 if an event happens and 0 otherwise; its expectation is the event's probability.
Assumptions built into a model's architecture, such as a CNN's locality and weight sharing. Less bias needs more data; ViTs have less than CNNs.
The k-means objective: the sum over all points of the squared distance to their own cluster center (within-cluster sum of squares).
Using a trained model to make predictions on new feature vectors (also called prediction).
The surprise -log p of an outcome with probability p; in bits for log base 2, nats for natural log.
Parent entropy minus the weighted entropy of the children; how much a split reduces uncertainty about the label.
Building a new class from an existing one: class Child(Parent) gets all of Parent's methods.
IC: the required values of a PDE's solution at the starting time, such as u(0, x) = sin(pi x).
A join that keeps only the keys found in both tables; unmatched rows are dropped. The default of merge.
The data fed to a network, counted as layer 0; it has no weights.
An object made from a class. Counter(5) makes a new instance of Counter.
Segmentation that also separates objects of the same class (car 1, car 2), usually with one mask per detected object.
The constant b in a linear model, the prediction when every feature is 0; another name for the bias term.
Predicting at inputs inside the range covered by the training data.
IQR = Q3 - Q1, the spread of the middle half of the data; values beyond Q3 + 1.5 IQR or below Q1 - 1.5 IQR are often called outliers.
The event 'A and B': outcomes in both.
idf(t), large for rare words and small for common ones; scikit-learn's default is ln((1 + n)/(1 + df(t))) + 1 for n documents.
Recovering a model's unknown parameters from (noisy) data it produced, such as a source position from field measurements.
Dropout that rescales the surviving entries by 1/(1 - p) during training, so the layer is the identity at test time. PyTorch's nn.Dropout works this way.
A square matrix A with an inverse A^{-1} (A^{-1} A = I); equivalently full rank, or det A != 0.
Task points from 0 to 100: 100 (raw - baseline) / (Max Score - baseline), with Max Score the larger of 0.9 times the organizers' solution and the best submission.
Intersection over union (Jaccard index): area of overlap / area of union of two boxes or masks; 1 identical, 0 disjoint.
Computing v pi by applying the Bellman expectation backup to every state repeatedly until the values stop changing.
An object that hands out values one at a time through next() and is used up after one pass. Generators and the results of zip, map, filter and enumerate are iterators.
For a function from R^n to R^m, the m x n matrix of first partial derivatives, entry (i, j) = d g i / d x j.
For a concave f, f(E[Y]) = E[f(Y)] (reversed for convex f). With f = log it gives the ELBO bound.
JSD(p q) = KL(p m)/2 + KL(q m)/2 with m = (p + q)/2: symmetric, 0 only when p = q, at most log 2.
A library whose dump and load save and restore Python objects (built on pickle, efficient for big NumPy arrays). The cheat sheet uses it for fitted scikit-learn models.
Combining two tables by matching the values of a key column: each pair of rows with equal keys gives one row of the result. df.merge(other, on=key, how=...).
The column whose values are matched in a join, such as product code. Keys match only if they are equal values of the same type.
p(x, y) = P(X = x and Y = y) for two discrete random variables.
A text format for nested data (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, true/false/null). Its object keys are always strings.
The distance in input pixels between neighboring units of a layer's output: the product of all strides so far.
The browser interface for Jupyter notebooks, with tabs, a file browser and a terminal.
Cut the data into k folds; train on k - 1 folds and validate on the remaining one, k times; average the scores.
A clustering algorithm: from k starting centers, repeatedly assign each point to its nearest center, then move each center to the mean of its points.
An initialization for k-means: the first center uniformly at random, each next one drawn with probability proportional to the squared distance to the nearest chosen center.
kNN: a classifier that predicts the most common label among the k training points closest to the query point.
A website that hosts data-science competitions with public and private leaderboards.
The reduction argument keepdims=True, which keeps the reduced axis with length 1 (shape (n, 1) instead of (n,)) so the result broadcasts back against the original.
The small grid of weights a convolution slides over its input, also called a filter. In nn.Conv2d each output channel has a kernel of shape (in channels, k, k).
The process that runs a notebook's code and holds its variables; restarting it clears them.
A function K(x, z) equal to the dot product phi(x) . phi(z) of mapped features, computed without forming phi.
Replacing every dot product in an algorithm (such as the SVM) with a kernel, to get a nonlinear model at the cost of a linear one.
In attention, the vector k a position offers for matching; its dot product with a query gives the score.
Two files made together for SSH: a private key that stays with you and a public key you give to servers.
An argument passed by parameter name, as in f(x, shift=5).
A parameter after a lone in the def line; it can only be passed by name.
A point where a piecewise linear function changes slope; ReLU(x - t) has one at x = t.
The optimality conditions for inequality constraints: the gradient condition, multipliers = 0, and a multiplier can be nonzero only for an active constraint.
D KL(p q) = sum p j log(p j / q j) = H(p, q) - H(p); never negative, zero only for q = p, not symmetric.
Training a small student network on the soft probability outputs of a larger trained teacher network.
Stored keys and values of earlier positions, reused at each generation step. Size: 2 x layers x tokens x KV heads x head size x bytes.
x 1 = sum of x i .
The sum of absolute values of the weights added to the loss; sets small weights to exactly zero.
x 2 = square root of the sum of x i^2, the ordinary Euclidean length.
The sum of squared weights added to the loss; shrinks every weight but rarely makes one exactly zero.
The true class of a sample (or the true value it should match), stored as an integer 0 to k-1 for classification.
Training on t = (1 - eps) y + eps / K instead of the one-hot y, so the best logits stay finite and the model is less overconfident. nn.CrossEntropyLoss(label smoothing=eps).
The number lambda in grad f = lambda grad g at a constrained optimum; one per constraint.
The function f(x) - lambda g(x); its critical points give the candidates for a constrained optimum.
A one-expression function written inline, as in lambda x: x x. Common as the key= of sorted, min and max.
A model that gives the probability of the next token given the tokens before it; trained by next-token prediction.
Linear regression with an L1 penalty on the weights.
Looking up a name's value when a function runs rather than when it is created. Lambdas made in a loop all see the loop variable's final value; a default such as i=i freezes the current one.
Running the diffusion process in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder, then decoding; much cheaper than diffusing pixels.
The set of all possible latent vectors z, usually R^k.
An unobserved random variable, such as the code z in a VAE, that a model uses to explain the data.
A model that explains each data point by an unobserved z: draw z from a prior p(z), then x from p(x z).
The code z = f(x) an encoder produces (or that a generative model samples); its entries are not labeled by anyone.
The standard way to type math as text, for example \frac{a}{b} for a fraction. In a text cell it goes between $ signs (inline) or $$ signs (display).
The sample mean of iid draws approaches the true mean as n grows.
P(A) = sum over a partition B j of P(A B j) P(B j).
A group of neurons that read the same input; a fully connected layer computes phi(W x + b) with one row of W per neuron.

nn.LayerNorm(D): normalize each example over its last D features with its own mean and variance, then gamma x hat + beta. No running statistics; identical in train and eval mode. Used in transformers.
A model whose training step only stores the data and does all the work at prediction time, such as kNN.
A node of a tree with no question; it predicts the majority class (or mean label) of the training examples that reach it.
A tensor made directly rather than computed from other tensors. Only leaves that require grad get a .grad; model parameters are leaves.
z for z 0 and alpha z otherwise (default alpha = 0.01): a ReLU whose gradient is never exactly 0.
The numbers a model computes from training data in fit, such as weights or a mean.
An nn.Embedding(max len, d) indexed by position and added to the token embeddings (BERT, GPT-2). Undefined beyond max len.
A plot of training and validation error against training set size (or training time).
A hyperparameter that sets the size of each training update step.
A rule that changes the learning rate during training, such as StepLR (multiply by gamma every few epochs) or CosineAnnealingLR; scheduler.step() once per epoch.
Choosing w to minimize Xw - y ^2; solved by the normal equations X^T X w = X^T y.
k-fold cross-validation with k = n: each fold is a single example.
Weights with variance 1 / fan-in, so a layer keeps the variance of its inputs (the 2026 P7.2 answer sigma w = 1/sqrt(C)).
A join that keeps every row of the left table in its order, with NaN in the right table's columns where no key matches. merge(..., how="left").
An early CNN (1998, digits): two 5x5 convolutions with pooling, then three linear layers; 61,706 parameters on 32x32 inputs.
A contour line: the set of points where a function takes one fixed value. The gradient is perpendicular to it.
Retrieval by word overlap between query and document (TF-IDF, BM25); misses synonyms and paraphrases.
Dictionary order for strings: compare character by character using character codes. Digit strings do not sort like numbers ("10" < "9"), and uppercase letters come before lowercase.
P(evidence hypothesis); for a model, the probability of the observed data as a function of the parameters (maximized by maximum likelihood).
Attention with weights phi(q i) . phi(k j), computed as phi(Q) (phi(K)^T V) divided row by row by phi(Q) (phi(K)^T 1): O(T l d) time instead of O(T^2 d).
A classifier whose decision boundary is a hyperplane w . x + b = 0, such as logistic regression or the perceptron.
No vector in the set is a linear combination of the others.
For quantiles: with sorted values x 0..x {n-1} and position h = (n - 1)q, take x i + f(x {i+1} - x i), where i is the integer part of h and f its fraction.
A neural network layer computing y = W x + b, with W of shape (outputs, inputs).
A map with f(ax + by) = a f(x) + b f(y); every one is multiplication by a matrix.
Training only a new linear head on the frozen features of a pretrained model.
A model that predicts a number as a weighted sum of the features plus a constant: y hat = w . x + b.
E[aX + bY + c] = a E[X] + b E[Y] + c for any random variables, independent or not.
A labeled dataset that some hyperplane splits with every +1 example strictly on one side and every -1 example strictly on the other.
The rule for the distance between two clusters: single (closest pair), complete (farthest pair), average, or Ward (increase in inertia).
An ordered, changeable sequence, written [1, 2, 3].
Each output of a convolution depends only on a small window of the input, not on every input value.
The derivative of one box of a computational graph with respect to one of its direct inputs.
A point whose value is less than or equal to the values at all nearby points.
grad E {x ~ p theta}[f(x)] = E[f(x) grad log p theta(x)], from grad p = p grad log p; the basis of REINFORCE.
The log of the likelihood, a sum of log-probabilities over examples; same maximizer, no underflow.
Binary cross-entropy: -[y ln p + (1 - y) ln(1 - p)], minus the log of the probability given to the true label.
The logarithm of mel filterbank energies per frame; the standard input of speech and audio models such as Whisper.
ln(p / (1 - p)), the inverse of the sigmoid; logistic regression models the log-odds as w . x + b.
LSE(z) = log of the sum of e^(z j), computed stably as m + log sum e^(z j - m) with m = max(z). Log-softmax is z - LSE(z).
log sigma^2, what a VAE encoder outputs instead of sigma so that any real number is valid; sigma = exp(logvar / 2).
A classifier for labels 0/1 that predicts p = sigmoid(x . beta) and is trained by minimizing the binary cross-entropy, a convex loss.
The raw real-valued scores a classifier outputs, one per class, before softmax turns them into probabilities.
A table layout with one row per observation and one column per variable, such as one row per sale with its store, category and amount. Filtering, grouping and joining work on this shape.
Low-rank adaptation: freeze W and learn h = W x + (alpha / r) B A x with A (r x d in) random, B (d out x r) zero; r(d in + d out) parameters per matrix; merge W + (alpha / r) B A afterward.
A number that measures how wrong a model's predictions are. Training changes the parameters to make it small.
A plot of training (and validation) loss against steps or epochs; its shape shows learning-rate problems, underfitting and overfitting.
A function that turns predictions and labels into one number measuring how wrong the model is; training makes it small.
A matrix of rank at most k close to A; the best one keeps the k largest SVD terms.
Long short-term memory: an RNN with a cell state c t = f c (t-1) + i g and gates i, f, o. 4(HI + H^2 + 2H) parameters per layer in PyTorch.
Writing a program whose behavior is set by fitting numbers to data instead of hand-written rules.
The plain mean of a per-class metric over the classes; every class counts equally.
The plain mean of the per-class F1 scores, f1 score(y, p, average='macro'); always predicting the majority class scores at most about 0.5 for two classes.
Mean absolute error: the average of y - y hat .
Predicting the label that appears most often among a set of votes (neighbors in kNN, trees in a forest).
The L1 distance sum j a j - b j , the length of a path along grid lines.
Maximum a posteriori estimate: maximize likelihood times prior; a Gaussian prior on the weights gives an L2 penalty.
The torch.load argument that says where to put the loaded tensors; map location="cpu" loads a checkpoint saved on a GPU onto the CPU.
For a linear classifier, the distance from the decision boundary to the nearest training points; 1 / w in the SVM scaling.
The distribution of one variable alone, found by summing (or integrating) the joint distribution over the other.
p(x) = integral of p(x z) p(z) dz, the probability of the data with the latent variable averaged out; also called the evidence.
A plain-text way to format writing: for headings, bold , - for bullet lists, backticks for code. Colab text cells use it.
A sequence of random variables where each one, given the previous one, does not depend on anything earlier.
An MDP: states, actions and dynamics p(s', r s, a) that depend only on the current state and action.
The next state and reward depend only on the current state and action, not on the earlier history.
An array with one class id (or 0/1 for foreground) per pixel.
MAE: hide most image patches (75%), encode only the visible ones, and train a light decoder to reconstruct the hidden patches' pixels (MSE on masked patches).
MLM: choose 15% of tokens, replace 80% of those by [MASK], 10% by random tokens, keep 10%, and predict the originals; loss only at the chosen positions (labels -100 elsewhere).
One vector per sequence: the average of the token vectors at real positions only, sum(h mask) / sum(mask).
Pooling that keeps the largest value in each window: nn.MaxPool2d(k). Its gradient goes only to the position of the max in each window.
MLE: the parameter value that maximizes the likelihood of the observed data, e.g. k / n for a Bernoulli.
The average (1/n) times the sum of the values.
mAP: the mean over classes of average precision, the area under each class's precision-recall curve, at a stated IoU threshold (mAP@0.5) or averaged over thresholds 0.5 to 0.95 (COCO).
mIoU: the IoU between predicted and true masks computed for each class over the dataset, then averaged over classes.
Averaging a sequence's token vectors into one vector, for example emb(idx).mean(dim=1).
The average over queries of 1/(rank of the first correct document); 1 when every correct document is ranked first.
The loss (1/N) times the sum over samples of (prediction - target)^2.
A copy of the model whose weights are an exponential moving average of the student's; its predictions serve as consistency targets.
The middle value of sorted data (the mean of the two middle values for even n); barely moved by outliers.
A set of triangular filters with centers equally spaced on the mel scale; multiplying a power spectrum by it gives mel energies.
A frequency scale that matches perceived pitch, m = 2595 log10(1 + f/700): roughly linear below 1 kHz and logarithmic above.
A function defined inside a class. Called as obj.method(args); Python passes the object as self.
MRO: the order of classes Python searches for a method, shown by Cls. mro . super() calls the next class in the MRO of the object's own class, which is not always the parent.
Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients: a discrete cosine transform of the log-mel energies, a classic compact audio feature.
A metric computed once from TP, FP and FN summed over all classes; for single-label problems micro-F1 equals accuracy.
Rescaling a feature to [0, 1] with (x - min) / (max - min).
A random subset of the training examples (for example 32) used to estimate the gradient for one update.
min over G, max over D of V(D, G) = E data[log D(x)] + E z[log(1 - D(G(z)))]: D maximizes, G minimizes.
The solution of Ax = b with the smallest norm: A^T (A A^T)^{-1} b for A with independent rows.
A 0/1 feature that records whether a value was missing before imputation.
An entry with no data. pandas shows it as NaN (or None in object columns) and isna() finds it; a file loaded with keep default na=False shows it as the empty string instead.
Running most matrix products in a 2-byte float format (bfloat16 or float16) while keeping weights and sensitive steps in float32; torch.autocast manages it.
A GAN failure where the generator produces only a few distinct outputs, covering a small part of the data distribution.
A function from feature vectors to predictions with adjustable numbers (parameters) inside it.
Choosing among models or hyperparameter settings, using validation data or cross-validation.
An RL method that learns from experienced transitions without knowing (or learning) the dynamics p(s', r s, a).
A .py file that other code can import. Importing runs the file once and gives access to its functions and classes as attributes, like sub.f.
An optimizer that steps along a running velocity v <- mu v + g (theta <- theta - lr v); steady gradient directions speed up by up to 1/(1 - mu), zigzags cancel. SGD(momentum=0.9).
Estimating a probability or expectation by averaging over many random samples; the error shrinks like 1 / sqrt(n).
The sequence of means of every run of w consecutive values; computed fast from cumulative sums.
H attentions (heads) run in parallel, each on its own d k-sized projections; their outputs are concatenated and mixed by an output projection W O.
MLA (DeepSeek-V2): cache a small latent c = W DKV x per token; keys and values are up-projections of c, and those projections can be folded into the query and output projections.
MQA: H query heads share a single key head and a single value head, shrinking the KV cache by a factor of H.
A pandas index with several levels, such as (customer, category) after grouping by two columns. reset index() turns the levels into ordinary columns.
A neural network made of linear layers with activation functions between them (MLP for short).
One multiplication added to a running sum (MAC). A convolution performs H out W out C out (C in/g) k^2 of them.
Several measured numbers per time step (several channels, such as several sensors).
N(mu, Sigma) for random vectors: density contours are ellipses along the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix Sigma.
Able to be changed in place: lists, dicts, sets, NumPy arrays, DataFrames and tensors.
To change an object in place, so every name pointing at it sees the change.
Events that share no outcomes (also called disjoint); P(A and B) = 0.
A run of n consecutive tokens; unigrams are single words, bigrams pairs such as 'not good'.
The agg form new column=(source column, function), as in df.groupby("customer").agg(total=("amount", "sum")); it names each output column.
Not a number: the float value for an undefined result such as sqrt(-1) or 0/0. Any arithmetic with nan gives nan; test for it with np.isnan.
The unit of information for natural logs, used by ML losses.
NLL, minus the log-likelihood, used as a loss; Gaussian noise gives squared error, Bernoulli labels give cross-entropy.
An outer cross-validation loop that scores the whole tuning procedure, with an inner cross-validation inside each outer fold for tuning.
A model made of layers, each feeding the next; with activation functions between the layers it can compute nonlinear functions.
The smallest unit of a neural network: a linear step w . x + b followed by an activation function.
The update w <- w - H^(-1) gradient, which jumps to the minimum of the second-order Taylor model. One step solves a quadratic exactly.
The original BERT's second task: predict from [CLS] whether sentence B follows sentence A. RoBERTa dropped it.
The language-model objective: at each position predict the following token; targets are the inputs shifted by one.
A list of modules that registers every layer, so their parameters count and train. Use it instead of a Python list when forward needs a loop.
A tensor wrapped as a learnable number of a module. Assigned to self.name in init , it is registered: it appears in parameters(), trains, and is saved in state dict. requires grad is True by default.
A container module that feeds its input through the given layers in order. Its parameters are named by position: 0.weight, 2.bias.
One box of a decision tree: an internal node asks a question; a leaf stores a prediction.
A command prefix that makes a program ignore the hangup signal, so it keeps running after the session ends.
The random part of a label that no function of the inputs can predict, as in y = f(x) + noise.
The lowest expected error any model can reach on new data because the noise cannot be predicted. For MSE it equals the noise variance.
In DBSCAN, a point that is neither core nor border; labeled -1.
Training a diffusion network eps theta(x t, t) to output the noise that produced x t; the loss is eps - eps theta ^2.
The list beta 1 .. beta T of per-step noise variances in a diffusion model (DDPM: linear from 1e-4 to 0.02 over T = 1000).
NMS: keep the highest-scoring box, delete the boxes overlapping it by more than an IoU threshold, repeat; done per class.
A Round 2 problem made of fixed parts with definite answers (derivations, shape and count questions, modules to implement, a training part), each part scored on its own.
The GAN generator loss -log D(G(z)) (BCE with fakes labeled 1), used instead of log(1 - D(G(z))), which is flat when D rejects the fakes.
Choosing parameters theta to minimize sum i (y i - g(x i; theta))^2 when g is nonlinear in theta; solved iteratively from a starting guess (scipy.optimize.curve fit).
A length of a vector. With no subscript it means the L2 norm.
The bell-curve distribution with a mean and a standard deviation; values cluster around the mean.
A^T A c = A^T x: the condition that the residual x - Ac is orthogonal to every column of A.
A raw metric turned into a number between 0 and 1. SP5 uses max(120 - MSE, 0) / 120, so MSE 0 scores 1 and any MSE of 120 or more scores 0.
A document made of code cells and text cells, saved as an .ipynb file.
Normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy: for each of the 2N views, cross-entropy over the other 2N - 1 views of cosine similarity / tau, with the partner view as the correct class.
A special 'no condition' input (an extra class or an empty prompt) used in classifier-free guidance training and sampling.
All x with Ax = 0.
Number of elements: t.numel() is the number of entries of a tensor. sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) counts a model's parameters.
Computed in a way that gives correct answers despite float limits such as overflow, underflow and rounding.
Half the sampling rate: the highest frequency a sampled signal can represent.
Finding every object in an image and giving each a class and a bounding box.
The dtype pandas gives a column of Python strings (or mixed Python objects). It prints as object, not str.
p / (1 - p) for an event of probability p; odds of 3 mean 3 to 1, p = 0.75.
Learning the values of a target policy (often greedy) from data generated by a different behavior policy (Q-learning, DQN).
Learning the values of the same policy that generates the data (SARSA).
Turning an integer label c out of k classes into a length-k vector with 1 at position c and 0 elsewhere.
Treating one class as positive and all other classes as negative, to get per-class metrics.
A Part 2 problem where you choose and train any model you like, and it is scored on a hidden test set.
A model whose trained weights are published, so you can run and fine-tune it on your own hardware (Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral).
For a fixed generator, D (x) = p data(x) / (p data(x) + p g(x)); it is 1/2 everywhere when p g = p data.
A policy whose value is at least as large as every other policy's in every state; it is greedy with respect to q .
v (s) = max over policies of v pi(s), and q (s, a) likewise; shared by all optimal policies.
The PyTorch object (such as torch.optim.SGD) that updates a model's parameters from their gradients; zero grad() clears the stored gradients.
An argument starting with - or -- that changes what a command does, such as -l in ls -l. Also called a flag.
Coding ordered categories as 0, 1, 2, ...; reasonable only when the order and spacing are real.
The default name Git gives the remote a repository was cloned from.
A square matrix Q with Q^T Q = I (orthonormal columns); a rotation or reflection.
Vectors whose dot product is 0 (perpendicular).
Unit length and mutually orthogonal. A matrix Q with orthonormal columns has Q^T Q = I.
A word a word-level tokenizer never saw; it becomes the unknown token [UNK]. Subword tokenizers avoid this by splitting rare words into pieces.
The training examples left out of a model's bootstrap sample (about 36.8%); predicting each example with the models that never saw it gives the OOB score.
One possible result of a random experiment.
For vectors u and v, the matrix u v^T whose entry (i, j) is u i v j. In NumPy: u[:, None] v[None, :].
A value far from the bulk of the data. The IQR rule flags values above Q3 + 1.5 IQR or below Q1 - 1.5 IQR.
A target far from the rest. Under MSE its gradient grows with its error and can dominate training; under MAE or Huber it counts like any other mistake.
The last layer of a network; it usually has no activation and outputs real numbers or logits.
The linear layer W O (H d v to d model) that mixes the concatenated head outputs in multi-head attention.
A debugging check: train on 10 to 20 examples; a correct model and loop drive the loss near 0, so if it does not, the bug is in the code.
The model fits noise in its training data: training error is low and validation error much higher.
Choosing submissions by their public score until the choice fits the luck of the public rows; the private score then falls short.
A float result too large to store, which becomes inf (np.exp(1000.0) is inf).
To define, in a subclass, a method with the same name as the parent's, so the subclass's version is used.
The user a file belongs to; the first set of permissions applies to this user.
A folder of modules that can be imported, such as torch; torch.nn is a submodule inside it.
Zeros added around the input before a convolution or pooling window slides: p rows above and below and p columns on each side, so H becomes H + 2p.
Appending a pad id to shorter sequences so a batch forms one rectangular (B, T) tensor.
Semantic and instance segmentation together for every pixel of the image.
A number inside a model that training chooses, such as a weight or the bias.
A list of dicts passed to an optimizer, each with its own params and options (for example weight decay=0 for biases).
PEFT: keep the pretrained weights frozen and train a small number of added parameters (adapters, prompt tuning, LoRA).
A model's adjustable numbers, such as weights and biases. Training changes them to make the loss small.
A family of distributions p(x; theta) indexed by a parameter theta, such as Bernoulli(p) or N(mu, sigma^2).
The class a subclass inherits from (also called the base class).
To read text and turn it into a value of another type, such as the string "2.5" into the float 2.5.
The derivative of a function of several inputs with respect to one of them, holding all the others fixed.
PDE: an equation relating an unknown function of several variables to its partial derivatives, such as the heat equation u t = alpha u xx.
Events that are disjoint and together cover the sample space, so every outcome is in exactly one.
In a ViT, one P x P square of the image across all C channels, flattened to C P^2 numbers. An H x W image has HW / P^2 patches.
The shared linear map from each flattened patch to a d-vector; equal to Conv2d(C, d, kernel size=P, stride=P) followed by flatten(2).transpose(1, 2).
The name of a file or directory in the file tree, with directories separated by /.
In early stopping, the number of epochs without a new best validation loss to wait before stopping.
Principal component analysis: project centered data onto the top-k eigenvectors of its covariance matrix (equivalently, the top right singular vectors of X c).
How far a candidate function is from satisfying a PDE at a point, for the heat equation u t - alpha u xx; a PINN minimizes its mean square.
Probability density function f of a continuous random variable: probabilities are areas under f. f can exceed 1.
Subtracting each series' own mean and dividing by its own standard deviation, X.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True); removes offset and gain differences.
The q-th percentile is the value below which q% of the data lie; np.percentile interpolates linearly between sorted values.
A linear classifier with labels -1/+1 trained by the rule: on a mistake y(w . x + b) <= 0, add y x to w and y to b.
The shift P after which a periodic function repeats. sin(2 pi x) has period 1.
A function that repeats: f(x + P) = f(x) for every x, for some period P 0.
The numbers 0, 1, ..., n-1 in some order. rng.permutation(n) returns a random one.
Reordering the inputs reorders the outputs the same way and changes nothing else. Self-attention without positional encodings is permutation equivariant.
t-SNE's setting for the effective number of neighbors each point's Gaussian bump covers (typically 5 to 50).
e^(mean negative log-likelihood per token). A uniform model over V tokens has perplexity V; lower is better.
PINN: a network u theta(t, x) trained so that its PDE residual (computed with autograd) and its initial and boundary errors are small; the physics is in the loss, not the architecture.

Python's standard way to save almost any object as bytes (pickle.dump, pickle.load with files opened in binary mode). It stores an object's class by module and name, so the class must be importable when loading.
Process ID: the number the system gives a running process; kill PID stops it.
A function that is affine on each of finitely many regions; every ReLU network computes one.
The symbol between two commands: the output of the first becomes the input of the second.
A chain of preprocessing steps and a model that is fit and applied as one unit, so transforms are fit on training data only.
A wrapper that bundles tokenizer, model and post-processing for one task, such as pipeline('sentiment-analysis').

A wide table built from long data: the distinct values of one column become the rows, those of another become the columns, and each cell aggregates a value column over the rows with that pair of keys (pandas pivot table).
The fraction of pixels labeled correctly; misleading when one class (background) covers most pixels.
Probability mass function p(x) = P(X = x) of a discrete random variable; its values sum to 1.
The agent's behavior pi(a s): a probability for each action in each state (deterministic if one action has probability 1).
An RL method that learns a parameterized policy pi(a s, theta) directly by gradient ascent on the expected return.
The policy that is greedy with respect to q pi is at least as good as pi in every state.
Alternating full policy evaluation with greedy policy improvement until the policy stops changing; it ends at an optimal policy.
K(x, z) = (x . z + c)^p, the dot product of all monomial features up to degree p.
BertModel's (B, d) output: the [CLS] vector passed through a linear layer and tanh.
A layer that slides a window over each channel and applies a fixed function (max or mean) instead of learned weights. No parameters; the channel count is unchanged. Default stride = kernel size.
The distribution that generates the data; its mean and variance are fixed but unknown.
A numbered entry point on a computer; each network service listens on its own (SSH on 22 by default).
Carrying connections to a port on one machine through an SSH connection to a port on another (ssh -L).
The two-layer network Linear(d, d ff), GELU, Linear(d ff, d) inside a transformer block, applied to every position with the same weights.
Position information added to a transformer, which otherwise treats its input as a set: learned or sinusoidal vectors added to the input, or relative terms inside the attention scores.
In binary classification, the class being detected (label 1), such as spam or fraud.
x^T A x 0 for every non-zero x; for symmetric A, all eigenvalues are positive.
Two views (or an image and its caption) that should get similar embeddings; every other pairing in the batch is a negative.
x^T A x = 0 for every x; for symmetric A, all eigenvalues are at least 0. X^T X always is.
LN(x + Sublayer(x)), the 2017 transformer's layout. Every path passes through a norm; harder to train deep without warmup.
The probability of a hypothesis after seeing the evidence, P(H E), computed with Bayes' rule.
A VAE failure where the KL term wins, the encoder outputs the prior for every input, and z carries no information about x.
A method for the eigenvector whose eigenvalue has the largest absolute value: repeat x <- Ax / Ax . The error shrinks like lambda 2 / lambda 1 ^k.
The values z = W x + b of a layer before the activation function is applied.
x + Sublayer(LN(x)): the layer norm is inside the residual branch, so the identity path never passes through a norm. Needs a final layer norm. Used by GPT-2 and most later models.
Of the examples predicted positive, the fraction that are actually positive: TP / (TP + FP).
The plot of precision against recall over all thresholds; more informative than ROC when positives are rare.
Estimating the value function v pi or q pi of a fixed policy, as opposed to control (finding a good policy).
VE(w) = sum s mu(s) [v pi(s) - v hat(s, w)]^2, the squared value error weighted by how often each state occurs.
The running total s t = x 0 + ... + x t (inclusive) for every t; torch.cumsum. Causal linear attention uses prefix sums of phi(k j) v j^T and phi(k j).
Turning raw data into a clean numeric feature matrix: imputing, encoding, scaling.
A model whose parameters were already trained, usually on a large dataset such as ImageNet, and are reused for a new task.
Training a model on a large unlabeled corpus with a self-supervised objective (masked or next-token prediction) before adapting it to a task.
A unit direction along which a dataset varies the most (computed in the PCA lesson).
The probability of a hypothesis before seeing the evidence, such as a base rate P(D).
The secret half of a key pair. Never share it; keep it at permission 600 or ssh refuses to use it.
The ranking by score on the remaining test rows, revealed at the end; it is the final result.
A function P on events with P(A) = 0, P(sample space) = 1, and P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) for disjoint A, B.
A running program. Each one has a PID and belongs to a user.
The approved adult at your test site who supervises the contest, gives the site code, and is the only one who can remove a temporary lock.
The closest point to x in a line or subspace; for a unit vector e it is (x . e) e.
A small MLP after the encoder whose outputs z feed the contrastive loss; it is discarded after pretraining and the encoder's h is used.
P = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T, which projects onto the column space of A; symmetric with P^2 = P.
x minus its projection; it is orthogonal to the line or subspace projected onto.
The shortcut of a residual block whose output shape differs from its input: a 1x1 convolution with the block's stride plus batch norm (downsample in torchvision).
The text given to a model as input; for CLIP zero-shot, a sentence such as 'a photo of a dog.' per class.
Averaging the embeddings of several prompt templates per class (then normalizing) to get a better class embedding.
Training a few learned vectors prepended to the input sequence while the model stays frozen.
For a loss = smooth part + L1 penalty: take a gradient step on the smooth part, then soft-threshold by (learning rate x lambda). Also called ISTA; it trains lasso with exact zeros.
Removing branches from a grown decision tree to reduce overfitting.
A^+ (np.linalg.pinv): A^+ b is the minimum-norm least-squares solution of Ax = b.
A label for an unlabeled example taken from a model's own confident prediction.
Self-training: predict the unlabeled data, keep confident predictions as labels (pseudo-labels), and retrain on them with the labeled data.
A fixed algorithm whose output looks random. The same seed always produces the same sequence.
The shareable half of a key pair; a server that lists it lets in whoever holds the matching private key.
The ranking by score on one part of the test rows, shown during a competition.
Off-policy TD control: Q(S, A) <- Q(S, A) + alpha [R + gamma max a Q(S', a) - Q(S, A)]; it estimates q while behaving epsilon-greedily.
LoRA with the frozen base weights stored in 4 bits, so a large model fits in less GPU memory.
Error that is roughly squared each step, so the number of correct digits about doubles; Newton's method near a minimum.
x^T A x for a symmetric matrix A, a sum of terms A ij x i x j.
A value with a given fraction q of the data below it, such as the 0.75 quantile. pandas and NumPy default to linear interpolation between sorted values.
The quantiles at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, written Q1, Q2 (the median) and Q3.
In attention, the vector q of a position that is matched against every key to decide where that position reads from.
R^2 = 1 - SS res / SS tot: 1 is perfect, 0 is no better than predicting the mean, negative is worse.
Anything with an uncertain result, such as rolling a die or drawing a training example at random.
Bagged decision trees in which every split chooses among a random subset of the features, which makes the trees less correlated.
Trying a fixed number of randomly sampled hyperparameter combinations.
A number determined by the outcome of a random experiment (formally, a function from outcomes to numbers).
The dimension of the column space: the number of independent columns (equal to the number of independent rows).
The position of a value in sorted order, starting at 1. With ties, the method decides: "min" gives ties the smallest position (1, 1, 3), "dense" (1, 1, 2), "average" (1.5, 1.5, 3).
rank(A) + dim null(A) = number of columns of A.
A non-zero outer product u v^T; every column is a multiple of u.
For a unit vector x, the number x^T A x. When x is an eigenvector it equals the eigenvalue, sign included.
Radial basis function (Gaussian) kernel exp(-gamma x - z ^2): 1 for identical points, near 0 for distant ones; larger gamma means narrower bumps.
Of the actual positives, the fraction predicted positive: TP / (TP + FN). Also called sensitivity or true positive rate.
In retrieval, the fraction of queries whose correct document is among the top k results.
The patch of input pixels that can affect one unit of a feature map. After layer l: r l = r (l-1) + (k eff - 1) j (l-1), starting from r 0 = 1.
Mapping scores back to the original space, Z W k^T + mean: the projection of each point onto the kept subspace.
A loss measuring how far the reconstruction x hat is from the input x, usually squared error summed over coordinates (or per-pixel BCE).
RNN: a network that reads a sequence one position at a time, updating a hidden state h t = tanh(W ih x t + W hh h (t-1) + b) with the same weights at every step.
Sending a command's output to a file: replaces the file's contents, appends to them.
An operation that turns many numbers into fewer, such as sum, mean, max or argmax, either over the whole array or along an axis.
The loss argument that says how per-entry losses combine: 'mean' (default), 'sum', or 'none' (return them all).

What nn.Module does when you assign an nn.Parameter or a module to self.name: it records it, so parameters(), state dict() and print(model) include it. Plain tensors and Python lists are not registered.
Predicting a number (rather than a class) for each sample.
A pattern language for text in which some characters are special; the dot matches any character. str.contains uses one unless you pass regex=False.
Any change to training that stops a model from fitting its training data too closely, most often a penalty on the weights.
The hyperparameter lambda that multiplies the penalty; larger lambda means a simpler model.
Monte Carlo policy gradient: after each episode, theta <- theta + alpha (G t - b) grad log pi(A t S t, theta) for every step t.
An agent learns which actions to take in an environment from numerical rewards, with no correct answer given per step.
A path read from the working directory, such as data/train.csv or ../models.
Position information that depends only on the offset j - i between query i and key j, for example scores q i . (k j + r (j-i)); 2T - 1 learned vectors for length T.
The function max(0, x) applied to every entry. Neural networks use it between layers.
Another copy of a repository, usually on GitHub, that you push commits to and pull commits from.
Writing a sample as z = mu + sigma eps with eps ~ N(0, I) drawn separately, so gradients flow to mu and sigma through backpropagation.
The store of recent transitions (s, a, r, s', done) that experience replay samples from; often a deque with a maxlen.
A project folder whose history Git tracks, kept in a hidden .git folder inside it. Also called a repo.
Converting a waveform to a different sampling rate, with filtering to avoid aliasing.
Changing a table between long and wide format without changing its numbers, with pivot table, unstack, stack or melt.
The difference between a target and the model's prediction for one sample, such as r n = y n - theta^T x n.
A block of layers F with a residual connection around it; the unit ResNets are built from.
Adding a block's input to its output, y = ReLU(F(x) + x), also called a skip connection. The block only has to learn the change F, and gradients flow straight through the addition.
The running sum carried from block to block in a transformer: the input embedding plus every sublayer's update so far.
A table with one row per experiment: what changed and the validation score. It guides the next experiment and becomes the report.
Finding the documents in a corpus most relevant to a query, usually by scoring every document and keeping the top k.
Answering with a language model after retrieving relevant documents and putting them into its prompt.
G t = R {t+1} + gamma R {t+2} + gamma^2 R {t+3} + ..., the discounted sum of future rewards; G t = R {t+1} + gamma G {t+1}.
The learned chain p(x {t-1} x t) = N(mu theta(x t, t), sigma t^2) that a diffusion model runs from noise to data.
In RL, the number R {t+1} the environment returns after action A t; the agent tries to maximize their discounted sum.
G t, the return from step t on, used in place of the whole-episode return G 0 to weight grad log pi(A t S t).
Linear regression with an L2 penalty on the weights.
Root mean squared error, the square root of the MSE; in the label's units.
An optimizer that divides each gradient by the square root of a running average of its squares, so every parameter moves about lr per step.
The plot of true positive rate against false positive rate over all thresholds.
The current row plus a fixed number of rows just before it. s.rolling(3, min periods=2).mean() averages the present values in each such window and gives NaN when fewer than 2 are present.
The first node of a decision tree, which every example passes through.
The top of the Linux file tree, written /. Every absolute path starts there.
The administrator account of a Linux system, allowed to change any file; sudo runs one command as root.
Rotary position embedding: rotate pair i of q and k at position m by angle m theta i. Then (R m q) . (R n k) = q . R (n-m) k depends only on n - m. No parameters; not applied to v.
Summarization metrics of n-gram overlap with a reference (ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2) or of the longest common subsequence (ROUGE-L), reported as recall, precision or F1.
Python's rule for round(): a value exactly halfway between two integers goes to the even one. round(2.5) is 2, round(3.5) is 4.
The span of the rows of A, the column space of A^T. It is orthogonal to the null space.
The order NumPy reads and fills entries in reshape: row by row, with the last axis changing fastest.
Batch norm's buffers running mean and running var: exponential moving averages of batch statistics (momentum 0.1, unbiased variance) used in eval mode.
The Python process on a Google machine that runs a notebook's cells. Variables, imports and functions live in its memory, not in the notebook file.
A critical point that is a minimum along some directions and a maximum along others, such as the origin for x^2 - y^2.
Padding that keeps the output the same size as the input at stride 1: p = (k - 1)/2 for an odd kernel, d(k - 1)/2 with dilation d. padding='same' in PyTorch.
One example in a dataset (one patient, one image). In a data table X of shape (n, d), each row is a sample.
The set of all possible outcomes, written Omega. Two dice have 36 ordered outcomes.
The file an open-ended problem gives to show the exact prediction format: column names, row ids and their order. Your CSV must match it.
The variance computed with n - 1 in the denominator instead of n (np.var(x, ddof=1)).
A number s i = 0 saying how much example i counts in a weighted loss; weight 2 acts like two copies, weight 0 removes it.
Samples per second of a waveform, in Hz; speech models expect 16,000 Hz.
On-policy TD control: Q(S, A) <- Q(S, A) + alpha [R + gamma Q(S', A') - Q(S, A)], with A' the action actually taken next.
The flat region of an activation such as sigmoid or tanh for large z , where the derivative is near 0 and little gradient passes through.
x . e for a unit vector e: the signed length of x along e.
softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d k)) V, row by row. The scale keeps scores at variance about 1 so the softmax does not saturate.
A classifier's number for an example, higher meaning more likely positive (often an estimated probability).
grad log pi(a s, theta); its expectation under pi is 0. For a softmax over logits it is one hot(a) - pi.
IOAI's scores on the validation data, given after each submission during the contest.
IOAI's scores of each final solution on the test data, computed after the contest; rankings and medals use only these.
The coordinates of the data along the principal components, Z = X c W k, shape (n, k).
A plot of the covariance eigenvalues (or explained variance ratios) in decreasing order, used to choose how many components to keep.
The integer that sets a random number generator's starting point, e.g. np.random.default rng(2026). Same seed, same numbers.
The first parameter of every method: the object the method is working on. Python fills it in automatically.
Attention where queries, keys and values all come from the same sequence, Q = X W Q^T, K = X W K^T, V = X W V^T.
Learning from unlabeled data by creating targets from the data itself, such as predicting the next word.
Giving every pixel of an image a class label; the output is logits (B, K, H, W) and the target a mask (B, H, W).
An update that differentiates only the prediction and treats a bootstrapped target as a constant (detach it in code).
Training on a small labeled set plus a larger unlabeled set from the same distribution.
One fixed-length vector per text, trained so that texts with similar meaning have vectors with high cosine similarity.
A special token such as that marks where a span was removed in T5's span corruption.
An ordered list x 0, ..., x (T-1) where order matters, such as the tokens of a sentence or the readings of a sensor over time.
T, the number of positions in a sequence. A batch of sequences has shape (B, T) as ids or (B, T, d) as vectors.
A task whose input and output are both sequences of possibly different lengths: translation, summarization, speech recognition.
One pandas column: a sequence of values plus an index label for each value. df["amount"] is a Series.
A computer that other computers connect to over the network, such as a shared GPU machine.
An unordered collection of distinct values, written {1, 2}. len(set(xs)) counts distinct values.
A large change in ranks between the public and the private leaderboard.
A new outer container holding the same inner objects, made by list(a), a[:], a.copy() or dict(d).
The tuple of an array's lengths along each axis, e.g. (2, 3) for 2 rows and 3 columns. Read it with a.shape.
A product AB needs columns of A = rows of B; then (m x n)(n x p) = (m x p).
The program inside a terminal that reads each command line and runs it; Ubuntu's default is bash.
The FFT of each windowed frame of a signal; its magnitude over time is the spectrogram.
The function 1 / (1 + e^(-z)), which squashes any real number into (0, 1). Logistic regression uses it to turn a score into a probability.
The mean over points of (b - a) / max(a, b), with a the mean distance to the own cluster and b to the nearest other cluster; from -1 to 1, higher is better.
A contrastive method: two augmented views per image, an encoder, a projection head, and the NT-Xent loss over the batch.
For unit-length rows W, S = W W^T: entry (i, j) is the cosine similarity of items i and j, with 1 on the diagonal.
A square matrix that is not invertible (determinant 0).
A diagonal entry sigma i of Sigma in the SVD; sigma i^2 are the eigenvalues of A^T A.
SVD: A = U Sigma V^T with U, V orthogonal and Sigma diagonal with sigma 1 = sigma 2 = ... = 0.
The columns of U (left) and V (right) in the SVD; A v i = sigma i u i.
Fixed PE[p, 2i] = sin(p w i), PE[p, 2i+1] = cos(p w i) with w i = 10000^(-2i/d). A shift by k positions is a fixed rotation of each pair.
In a U-Net, concatenating an encoder feature map with the decoder map of the same size, so fine detail lost by pooling reaches the output.
xi i = 0, how far example i falls short of the margin condition y i f(x i) = 1 in a soft-margin SVM.
An index of the form start:stop:step. The stop is excluded, and a slice keeps its axis even when it has length 1.
1 minus the Dice coefficient computed with predicted probabilities instead of hard masks, usually per class with smoothing and averaged over classes.
A training target that is a probability vector (or a probability between 0 and 1) rather than a one-hot label.
The L1 solution w = sign(a) max( a - lambda, 0): move a toward zero by lambda and stop at zero.
An SVM that allows margin violations, each costing C times its slack: minimize w ^2 / 2 + C sum of hinge losses.
The map from scores z to probabilities e^(z i) / sum j e^(z j). Subtracting max(z) first gives the same result without overflow.
pi(a s) = softmax of per-action scores (action preferences) computed by a network; the RL version of a classifier's logits.
Logistic regression for K classes: logits Z = XW + b, probabilities softmax(Z) row by row, trained with cross-entropy; gradient X^T (P - Y) / n.
The function ln(1 + e^z), a smooth version of ReLU whose derivative is the sigmoid.
The set of all linear combinations of some vectors.
T5's pretraining task: replace random spans of the input by sentinel tokens and train the decoder to output each sentinel followed by its span.
Having many entries exactly equal to zero.
A matrix stored as only its nonzero entries and their positions (SciPy's CSR format); text features are mostly zeros.
Augmentation for spectrograms: masking random bands of time steps and of frequency bins during training.
A reserved id that is not text, such as [PAD], [CLS], [SEP], [MASK] (BERT ids 0, 101, 102, 103) or GPT-2's .
The recall of the negative class: TN / (TN + FP).
Clustering by building a similarity graph, embedding points with the eigenvectors of its Laplacian for the smallest eigenvalues, then running k-means.
Every real symmetric matrix is Q Lambda Q^T with Q orthogonal and Lambda real diagonal.
A time-frequency picture of a signal: the power (or magnitude) of each frequency bin in each frame.
A node's question 'x j <= t?' that sends each example to the left or right child.
The groupby pattern: split the rows into groups by a key, apply a computation to each group, combine the results into one table indexed by the key.
Single shot detector: predicts boxes from feature maps at several resolutions, coarse maps for large objects and fine maps for small ones.
Secure shell: an encrypted connection to another computer that gives you a shell on it.
The file ~/.ssh/config, where a short alias can stand for a host, user, port and key.
A text-to-image latent diffusion model: VAE latents, a U-Net denoiser reading a text encoder through cross-attention, and classifier-free guidance.
A sort that keeps equal elements in their original order. Python's sorted and .sort are stable.
One of layer1 to layer4 in a torchvision ResNet: a Sequential of residual blocks at one resolution. Each stage after the first halves H and W and doubles the channels.
Git's snapshot of what the next commit will contain; git add copies files into it. Also called the index.
The vectors e j with a 1 in position j and 0 elsewhere. Column j of a matrix is the image of e j.
The square root of the variance. It measures spread in the data's own units.
The standard deviation of an estimate: sigma / sqrt(n) for a mean, sqrt(p (1 - p) / n) for a proportion.
N(0, 1), the normal distribution with mean 0 and variance 1, usually written Z.
Rescaling a feature to mean 0 and standard deviation 1: z = (x - mean) / std, with statistics from the training set.
In RL, the description S t of the situation the agent observes at time t.
v pi(s) = E pi[G t S t = s], the expected return from state s when following policy pi.
model.state dict(): a dict from dotted names to tensors holding every registered parameter and buffer. torch.save it; load it into a model of the same architecture with load state dict.
A number computed from a sample, such as the sample mean.
alpha in an update V <- V + alpha (target - V): how far each estimate moves toward its target.
SGD: gradient descent using gradients from random mini-batches (or single examples) instead of the whole training set.
A policy that spreads probability over several actions in some state, pi(a s) < 1 for every a there.
Very common words (the, a, of) that some pipelines remove before counting.
The .str attribute of a Series of strings. s.str.strip(), s.str.lower() and so on run a string method on every value and return a new Series.
k-fold cross-validation in which every fold keeps the class proportions of the whole set.
Convex with strict inequality for distinct points; it has at most one minimizer. A positive definite Hessian everywhere is enough.
How many positions a convolution or pooling window moves at each step. Output size floor((H + 2p - d(k - 1) - 1)/s) + 1.
For each axis of an array, the number of bytes to move in memory to reach the next entry along that axis. Slicing and transposing change only the shape and strides, which is why they make views.
A class that inherits from another: in class Child(Parent), Child is a subclass of Parent.
A module stored as an attribute of another module. Its parameters count as the parent's, with dotted names like hidden.weight.
Tokenizing into pieces of words: frequent words are one token, rare words several. BPE (GPT) and WordPiece (BERT) are the two common kinds.
A few numbers that describe a column: count, mean, standard deviation, minimum, quartiles, maximum. df.describe() prints them.
Gives access to the parent class's version of a method from inside a subclass, as in super(). init ().
Learning from examples that come with labels, to predict the label from the features.
The number of examples whose true label is a given class.
SVM: a linear classifier sign(w . x + b) chosen to maximize the margin, by minimizing w ^2 / 2 subject to y i (w . x i + b) = 1.
The training points exactly on an SVM's margin; only they have nonzero multipliers and determine w.
One pass of backups over every state.
CLIP's loss: the mean of cross-entropy over rows (image to text) and over columns (text to image) of the similarity logits, with the diagonal as targets.
A square matrix equal to its transpose.
If all units of a layer start with the same weights they get the same gradients and stay identical forever; random initialization breaks the symmetry.
The first message of a chat, with instructions that apply to the whole conversation.
t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding: a nonlinear 2D map that matches neighbor probabilities by minimizing KL divergence; keeps neighborhoods, distorts gaps and cluster sizes.
Text-to-text transfer transformer: an encoder-decoder that casts every task as text to text, pretrained by span corruption.
The hyperbolic tangent (e^z - e^(-z)) / (e^z + e^(-z)), with values in (-1, 1) and derivative 1 - tanh^2(z).
The true value a model's prediction should match for one sample.
A copy of the Q-network, synced every C steps, used to compute DQN targets so that they do not move with every update.
The policy whose value function is being learned; in Q-learning, the greedy policy.
delta t = R {t+1} + gamma V(S {t+1}) - V(S t), the difference between the TD target and the current estimate.
R {t+1} + gamma V(S {t+1}) (just R {t+1} if S {t+1} is terminal): the one-step estimate of the return that TD moves toward.
Temporal-difference prediction: after each step, V(S t) <- V(S t) + alpha [R {t+1} + gamma V(S {t+1}) - V(S t)].
Training a sequence model on the true previous tokens instead of its own predictions.
tau in exp(similarity / tau); a small tau sharpens the softmax so the hardest negatives dominate the gradient.
tau in softmax(z / tau): tau 1 flattens it, tau - 0 is greedy.
Model-free learning from each step's reward plus the current estimate of the next state's value (TD(0), SARSA, Q-learning).
PyTorch's array type, like a NumPy array but able to record operations for autograd; torch.tensor(0.5) is a one-number tensor.
torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(X, y): a dataset whose item i is (X[i], y[i]); the tensors must share their first axis.
tf(t, d): how often word t occurs in document d (scikit-learn uses the raw count).
A text window where you type commands and read their output.
A state that ends an episode; no rewards follow it, so its value is 0.
Held-out data the model never saw during training, used only to measure how well it does.
Assigning one label to each text (spam or not, topic, sentiment).
Term frequency times inverse document frequency, usually with each document's vector scaled to unit L2 norm; down-weights words that occur everywhere.
The cutoff t: an example is predicted positive when its score is at least t.
Theta(z) = 1 if z = 0 and 0 if z < 0 (the step or Heaviside function); the 2026 paper used Theta(0) = 1.
A neuron Theta(w . x + b) that outputs 1 on one closed side of the hyperplane w . x + b = 0 and 0 on the other.
A vector encoding the diffusion step t (sinusoids, then an MLP) that is projected and added to the feature maps of each block.
A sequence of measurements in time order; a univariate dataset has shape (N, L), a multivariate one (N, C, L).
One tick t = 0, 1, 2, ... of the agent-environment loop: the agent sees S t, picks A t, then receives R {t+1} and S {t+1}.
Validation that always trains on earlier data and validates on later data.
Capital first letter on every word, the rest lowercase: str.title() turns "united kingdom" into "United Kingdom" (and "usa" into "Usa").
A program that keeps shell sessions running on a server after you disconnect; reattach later with tmux attach.
The unit of text a model reads (a character, a word or a piece of a word), stored as an integer id. Also used for each position's vector inside a transformer.
BERT's tokenizer output that marks which sentence (0 or 1) each token belongs to when two sentences are packed into one input.
The function that turns text into a list of token ids and back (encode and decode).
The largest difference still counted as equal when comparing floats, as in abs(a - b) <= 1e-9.
Keep the k largest logits, set the rest to -inf, renormalize, sample.
Nucleus sampling: keep the smallest set of most likely tokens whose probabilities sum to at least p (including the one that crosses p), renormalize, sample.
PyTorch's image library: standard models (torchvision.models), pretrained weights, datasets and image transforms. Installed in Colab.
The sum of the diagonal entries of a square matrix; it equals the sum of the eigenvalues.
The report Python prints for an uncaught exception: the chain of calls, oldest first, then the exception type and message on the last line.
Running an algorithm that chooses a model's parameters to make the loss on the training examples small (also called fitting).
The part of the data a model learns from.
The four lines repeated in every training loop: optimizer.zero grad(); loss = loss fn(model(X), y); loss.backward(); optimizer.step().
The sequence S 0, A 0, R 1, S 1, A 1, R 2, ... produced by an agent interacting with an environment.
Reusing a pretrained model's layers for a new task, typically by keeping its backbone and training a new head.
The repeated unit of a transformer: multi-head attention and a position-wise MLP, each inside a residual connection with a layer norm. 12d^2 + 13d parameters with biases and d ff = 4d.
Shifting the input shifts the output in the same way: a convolution (stride 1) finds a pattern wherever it is.
The matrix with rows and columns swapped: entry [i, j] moves to [j, i]. In NumPy A.T or np.transpose(A); it does nothing to a 1D array.
nn.ConvTranspose2d: a learned upsampling layer; with kernel 2 and stride 2 each input pixel becomes a 2 x 2 patch, doubling H and W.
TN: an actual negative predicted negative.
TP: an actual positive predicted positive.
TPR = TP / (TP + FN), the same as recall.
Dropping the fractional part of a number, moving toward zero. int(-2.7) is -2.
Cutting a token sequence that is longer than max length down to max length.

Whether a value counts as true in an if: zero (0, 0.0), None, False and empty strings or containers are falsy; every nonzero number (negative too) and every nonempty string or container is truthy. So if x % 2 keeps odd x.
A box of code in a lesson that you can edit and run. The last line's value is shown, as in a notebook cell.
An ordered sequence that cannot be changed after it is made, written (3, 4). Functions return several values as a tuple.
The kind of a value, such as int, float, bool, str, list or None. type(x) shows it.
A convolutional encoder-decoder with skip connections between matching resolutions; its output has the input's spatial size.
Universal function: a NumPy function such as np.exp, np.log or np.maximum that acts on every entry of an array.
Uniform manifold approximation and projection: a nonlinear map that lays out a nearest-neighbor graph in 2D; favors local neighborhoods over global distances.
An estimator whose expectation equals the true value; the n - 1 sample variance is unbiased, the divide-by-n one is not.
An autoencoder whose code is shorter than its input (k < d), so it cannot learn the identity map.
A linear system with fewer independent equations than unknowns; it has infinitely many solutions if it has any.
The model is too simple for the pattern: training and validation error are both high.
A positive float result too small to store, which becomes exactly 0 (np.exp(-2000.0) is 0.0).
Equal probability (or constant density) over a set; U(a, b) has density 1 / (b - a), mean (a + b) / 2, variance (b - a)^2 / 12.
The event 'A or B': outcomes in at least one of them.
A vector of norm 1; v / v is the unit vector in the direction of v.
One measured number per time step (one channel).

A network with one hidden layer and a non-polynomial activation (ReLU, sigmoid, tanh) can approximate any continuous function on a bounded region, given enough hidden units. It does not say how many, or whether training finds them.
Assigning the items of a sequence to several names at once: a, b = (1, 2).
Learning from examples with no labels, to find structure such as clusters.
A file in the working tree that Git has never been told to track; git status lists it with ??.
During backpropagation, the derivative of the loss with respect to a box's output, which the box multiplies by its local derivative.
A convolution with no padding, so the kernel only visits positions where it fits inside the input: output H - k + 1 at stride 1.
Held-out examples used to compare models and choose hyperparameters (also called the dev set).
In attention, the vector v a position hands over; the output is the weighted average of the values.
Repeating the Bellman optimality backup V(s) <- max a sum p [r + gamma V(s')] until convergence, then acting greedily.
In a deep network the gradient is a product of one factor per layer; if the factors are below 1 (sigmoid's derivative is at most 0.25), the early layers get almost no gradient and barely train.
The mean squared distance from the mean, (1/n) times the sum of (x i - mean)^2. This is the population variance.
Error from a model reacting to its particular training set: how much its predictions change from one training set to another.
Drawing a linear layer's weights with standard deviation 1/sqrt(in features), so each output has the same variance as each input (Var y = C sigma w^2 sigma^2).
A latent variable model with a neural decoder p(x z), a prior N(0, I) and an encoder q(z x), trained by maximizing the ELBO.
To replace a Python loop over entries with whole-array NumPy operations, which run far faster.
Keeping the history of a project's files so that any earlier version can be seen or restored.
A 2014 CNN family built from 3x3 convolutions with padding 1 and 2x2 max pools, channels 64 to 512; VGG-16 has 138 million parameters, mostly in its linear head.
An array that shares memory with another array, made by basic slicing, reshape, ravel or .T. Writing into a view changes the original.
In contrastive learning, one random augmentation (crop, flip, color jitter, blur) of an example; two views of one image form a positive pair.
ViT: a transformer encoder applied to an image cut into P x P patches, each patch a token, plus a class token and learned position embeddings.
The fixed list of tokens a tokenizer knows; its size V is the number of rows of the embedding table and the number of outputs of a language model.
Starting training with a small learning rate and raising it over the first steps or epochs, to avoid large early updates from random weights.
Audio as a 1-D array of amplitudes sampled at equal time steps (floats in [-1, 1] for most libraries).
A parameter that multiplies a feature, such as w in w size + b.
The name for L2 regularization in neural network training.
A convolution uses the same kernel at every position, so its parameter count does not depend on the image size.
Using the token embedding matrix (V x d) also as the output layer's weight, so the output layer adds no parameters (GPT-2, BERT).
The mean of a per-class metric weighted by each class's support.
The impurity of a split's children, each weighted by its share of the examples: (n L/n) I(left) + (n R/n) I(right).
OpenAI's encoder-decoder speech model: 30-second log-mel spectrograms in, text tokens out (transcription or translation to English).
Spaces, tabs and newlines. strip() removes it from both ends of a string, never from the middle.
A table layout with one row per entity and one column per value of a second key, such as one row per store and one column per category. pivot table produces it; melt turns it back into long format.
The number of units (neurons) in a layer.
A taper such as the Hann window multiplied into each frame before the FFT, to reduce leakage between frequency bins.
A vector per word, trained (as in word2vec or GloVe) so that words used in similar contexts get similar vectors.
BERT's subword tokenizer. It chooses merges by a likelihood score and marks pieces that continue a word with .
The directory the shell is in right now; pwd prints it and relative paths start from it.
The files on disk in a repository, the version you edit.
Glorot initialization: weights with variance 2 / (fan-in + fan-out), a compromise between the forward and backward passes; for tanh and sigmoid. Uniform bound sqrt(6 / (fan-in + fan-out)).
Exclusive or: (0,0), (1,1) in one class and (0,1), (1,0) in the other; the standard example of data no line can separate.
You only look once: a one-pass detector that predicts boxes, objectness and classes for every cell of an S x S grid.
Classifying into classes with no labeled training examples, for CLIP by comparing an image's embedding with embeddings of a text prompt per class.
Asking a language model to do a task from an instruction alone, with no worked examples.
